status_summary: Several Section 232 actions address the named sectors, but they are tariff and negotiation tools that cover all source countries, none names China, and they do not eliminate dependence on China. Proclamation 11002 (signed 2026-01-14) set a 25 percent duty on certain advanced computing chips with broad exemptions, Proclamation 11001 of the same date on processed critical minerals directed negotiations and left import restrictions as a later option, and Proclamation 11020 (signed 2026-04-02) set a 100 percent duty on imported patented pharmaceuticals, effective 2026-07-31 for listed companies and 2026-09-29 for others, with reduced or zero rates for companies with onshoring plans or pricing agreements and for certain partners, and exempted generics for now. On 2026-02-02 EXIM approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, a public-private strategic critical minerals reserve. In an arrangement reported 2025-11-01, China agreed to suspend its October 2025 rare earth export controls for one year and issue general licenses, which relies on continued Chinese supply rather than reducing it.

timeline.event: China agrees, in an arrangement with the United States, to suspend its October 2025 rare earth export controls for a year and issue general licenses (as reported by Fortune citing a White House fact sheet).
Proclamations 11001 (critical minerals, negotiations and possible price floors) and 11002 (25 percent duty on certain advanced chips) were published; both were signed 2026-01-14.
EXIM approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, a strategic critical minerals reserve.
